## The mission, verbatim

> (4) When — and only when — SES-197 is shipped and the roster is clean, name the M3 drain scope
> with SES-191 ordered ABOVE SES-182 (or SES-182 excluded), then declare the M3 drain. Do NOT
> declare it before the preconditions ship.

Items (1)–(3) of that directive shipped in the three cycles immediately before this one:
`v7.0.238` (SES-197), `v7.0.239` (SES-199..202 filed), `v7.0.240` (SE-01..SE-06 triaged). This
cycle is its last item, so the directive closes here.

## Premise, revalidated live this cycle (not recalled)

Both preconditions were read from live state before anything was written, because the directive
makes declaring early the one forbidden move:

- **SES-197 is shipped.** `backlog_items.status = 'done'`, and — the load-bearing half, since a
  status is a claim and a function is a fact — `select count(*) from pg_proc … proname =
  'drain_chain_gate'` returns **1**. The terminator exists in the database, not just on a card.
- **The roster is clean.** `v7.0.240` triaged SE-01..SE-06; five carry real titles and SE-05 is
  `removal proposed` awaiting John. Read live: `backlog_display_title()` falls back on none of
  the five.

## What was decided, and why it is the harder of John's two options

His sentence offers a choice: order `SES-191` above `SES-182`, **or** exclude `SES-182`. This
cycle took the **first**.

`SES-182` — *Auto-rollback on red* names its dependency on `SES-191` — *Full restore drill* in its
own text, and sat at queue **12** while `SES-191` sat at queue **334** — the inversion the M2 gate
review's Chief Architect lens flagged. Excluding `SES-182` would have removed the inversion by
removing the ticket, and M3 would then have been able to retire **without auto-rollback**, which
is the third of the three pillars the charter names for this milestone (portable CI, reviewer
lane, auto-rollback). Reordering fixes the dependency itself and keeps M3's finish line whole.

**The mechanism, and why this one:** `SES-191` was given `automation_rank = -27`, the lane slot
freed when `SES-197` went `done`. That is deliberately the *narrowest* write that satisfies the
instruction:

- `claim_automation_lane_top()` — the one sanctioned lane call — assigns `min(open lane) − 1`,
  which would have put `SES-191` at the top of the **whole board**, above `SES-203` and above the
  four tickets the gate review had just filed as M3's own precondition cleanup. The directive asks
  for `SES-191` above `SES-182`, not above everything.
- A `pinned_position` is John's tap and this cycle set none. Pins stay his.

Result, measured after the recompute: `SES-191` **#10**, `SES-180` #11, `SES-181` #12,
`SES-182` #13. The four review tickets keep #6–#9.

## The scope is a fixed list, not the live tier

Per `SES-142`, `runner_drain_scope` captures the members open **at naming time**, and a ticket
filed into M3 after this row never joins this drain. 23 rows were written:

`SES-199`, `SES-200`, `SES-201`, `SES-202`, `SES-191`, `SES-180`, `SES-181`, `SES-182`, `SES-77`,
`SES-71`, `SES-61`, `SES-58`, `SES-135`, `SES-130`, `SES-51`, `SES-45`, `SES-008`, `SE-06`,
`SE-01`, `SE-02`, `SE-03`, `SE-04`, `SE-05`.

**Four of the 23 cannot be closed by any cycle, and that is stated rather than hidden:**
`SES-181` and `SES-182` are `needs-john`, `SES-180` is `needs-desktop`, `SE-05` is
`removal proposed`. The drain therefore cannot retire until John acts on those four. Before
`SES-197` that would have been the infinite loop the gate review predicted; Gate C now stops the
chain at the first continuation whose only remaining work is a decision he owes.

## Authority note

`drain_epic_next()` property 5 — *nothing creates a drain row but John's own declaration, a
directive row or a briefing tap* — is satisfied by construction here: directive `1532666b` **is**
that declaration, and this cycle executed it rather than originating it. The standing prohibition
on a cycle creating a drain of its own initiative is untouched.

## QA — discriminating, with the negative control named

Would each assertion still pass if the change did nothing?

| # | Assertion | Result | On the pre-change state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Exactly one `queued` `drain-epic` row exists, epic = M3 | `6810599f`, 23 scope rows | none existed — `drain_epic_next()` returned `none` |
| 2 | `SES-191.queue` < `SES-182.queue` | **10 < 13** | 334 > 12 — inverted, fails |
| 3 | `drain_epic_next()` returns a real pick | `pick`, `SES-199` #6, `open_now = 23` | `none` |
| 4 | Scope contains `SES-182` (not the exclusion fallback) | present at #13 | n/a |

Assertions 1–3 all fail against the state this cycle started from, so the QA is measuring the
change rather than the platform. Pre-change values are not recalled: they are in this cycle's
`runner_before_images` row for `SES-191` (`automation_rank` NULL, queue 334).
